cant.s7.plan.summary.summary:
This plan describes how Tussock Rise Farm manages the risks its farming poses to freshwater, and the actions the owner will take to reduce them. It follows Schedule 7 of the Canterbury Land and Water Regional Plan.

The farm is 248 hectares on the Example Plains, of which 231.5 hectares are grazable. It carries sheep, beef cattle and dairy grazing and grows winter fodder crops on part of the cultivated area.

The highest risks are nitrate leaching on the light soils and terraces, and sediment, phosphorus and microbial loss from the creek flats during winter grazing.

Much of the stock exclusion fencing is done and nutrients are managed from an annual nutrient budget. The remaining actions are in the action table.
cant.s7.plan.summary.vision:
- Healthy waterways that stock and people can use
- Soils that stay on the farm and keep their structure
- Nutrients used by crops and pasture, not lost to water
- A farm business that can show its progress to neighbours and the council
cant.s7.plan.summary.farm_story:
Tussock Rise has been in the owner's family for three generations. It began as a dryland sheep farm and was developed for irrigation in the 1990s, when the groundwater consent was granted.

Today the farm runs sheep and beef cattle, grazes dairy heifers for neighbouring dairy farms and grows winter fodder crops. The owner lives on the property and employs one part-time worker during lambing and winter grazing.

The creek along the south-east boundary is the farm's main waterway. Fencing it and managing winter grazing near it are the owner's two biggest priorities.

cant.s7.property.areas.stock_summary: About 2,700 stock units: 480 dairy heifers, 70 beef cattle and 1,100 ewes

LU1.name: Irrigated Light Soils
LU1.description: Free-draining stony silt loams under centre pivot and lateral irrigation. These soils carry most of the farm's pasture and winter forage production.

LU2.name: Irrigated Heavy Soils
LU2.description: Deeper, slower-draining silt loams under centre pivot and border-dyke irrigation. They pug easily when wet and are used for most of the winter crop.

LU3.name: Dryland River Terraces
LU3.description: Very stony terraces with no irrigation. Pasture growth depends on spring and autumn rain and the land is mostly grazed by cattle.

LU4.name: Leased Creek Flats
LU4.description: Flat leased land along the south-east boundary beside the creek. It is poorly drained and is grazed seasonally under a lease.

cant.s7.nutrients.obj1.summary: Nutrients are matched to crop need from an annual budget, and losses are kept below the GMP Loss Rate.

cant.s7.nutrients.t1.how_met: Nitrogen loss is 21 kg N/ha/yr in the 2025/26 nutrient budget, below the Baseline GMP Loss Rate of 26 and the GMP Loss Rate of 22.

cant.s7.nutrients.t2.how_met: Winter crops are grazed from the top of the paddock down, and catch crops are sown after the winter crop on the light soils.

cant.s7.nutrients.t3.how_met: Critical source areas are left ungrazed in winter and a 10 m grass buffer is kept along the creek and drain.
cant.s7.nutrients.t3.records: Winter grazing plan; photos each July

cant.s7.nutrients.t4.how_met: Fertiliser rates come from soil tests every two years and the nutrient budget; no nitrogen is applied from 1 May to 31 July.
cant.s7.nutrients.t4.records: Soil tests; fertiliser recommendations and application records

cant.s7.nutrients.t5.how_met: Fertiliser is delivered to the bunded loading pad 80 m from the creek; spreading is by a Spreadmark-certified contractor.

cant.s7.irrigation.obj1.summary: Irrigation is scheduled to soil moisture and the system is checked every year.

cant.s7.irrigation.t1.not_applicable_reason: No new irrigation system is planned on this farm.

cant.s7.irrigation.t2.how_met: The pivots and the lateral are checked before the season and a uniformity test is done every year.
cant.s7.irrigation.t2.records: Annual system check; uniformity test reports

cant.s7.irrigation.t3.how_met: Irrigation is scheduled from soil moisture probes and the weekly water balance; application depth is set for each soil.

cant.s7.irrigation.t4.how_met: The owner and the part-time worker are trained by the irrigation supplier each spring.

cant.s7.soils.obj1.summary: Cultivation and winter grazing are planned to keep soil on the farm.

cant.s7.soils.t1.how_met: Winter grazing is planned around critical source areas and the creek flats are only grazed in dry conditions.

cant.s7.soils.t2.how_met: Cultivation is timed for dry soils, paddocks are re-sown before 31 March and stock come off wet paddocks at an agreed trigger.

cant.s7.waterbodies.obj1.summary: The creek and spring-fed drain are fenced, planted and kept clear of stock.

cant.s7.waterbodies.t1.how_met: The creek is fenced on one side; the remaining 400 m will be fenced by 1 March 2027.

cant.s7.waterbodies.t2.how_met: A 10 m grass margin is kept and 0.8 ha of the creek margin will be planted in natives.

cant.s7.waterbodies.t3.how_met: A culvert crossing will replace the ford at the main race; troughs are kept 20 m from the creek.

cant.s7.waterbodies.t4.how_met: Tuna and kōura habitat in the creek is protected by fencing, shade planting and no fertiliser in the setbacks.

cant.s7.point_sources.obj1.summary: One offal pit, to be moved; farm rubbish leaves the farm.

cant.s7.point_sources.t1.how_met: Farm rubbish is taken off site; the old offal pit will be moved more than 50 m from the bore and waterways before it is used again.
cant.s7.point_sources.t1.records: Pit location on the farm map

cant.s7.water_use.obj1.summary: Stock water is metered and leaks are fixed quickly.

cant.s7.water_use.t1.how_met: Stock water is float-controlled and leaks are fixed within a week; the main meter is verified every five years.

nz.catchment.context.summary: The farm drains to the Example Creek and to shallow groundwater under the Example Plains. Nitrate in groundwater and sediment in the creek are the catchment's main issues.
nz.catchment.context.receiving_environment: Example Creek, then the lower Example River and its estuary

nz.catchment.regard.response: Nitrogen loss is held below the GMP Loss Rate, the creek margin is being fenced and planted, and the offal pit is being moved away from the bore.

Land and soil.description: About fifty hectares of the irrigated heavy soils and the creek flats are cultivated in rotation for fodder beet and kale, then returned to pasture. Cultivation is timed for dry soils and kept away from the creek margin.
Land and soil.risks: Bare soil and winter grazing are the main routes for sediment and phosphorus loss. Critical source areas are left ungrazed and a back-fence is used, and a grass buffer is kept along every waterway.

Waterways and wetlands.activities: Stock exclusion, crossings, and riparian management
Waterways and wetlands.description: The creek along the south-east boundary is the farm's only permanent waterway. It is fenced on one side, with about four hundred metres still to do, and a small spring-fed drain feeds into it near the leased flats.
Waterways and wetlands.risks: Stock access, crossings and a lack of riparian cover are the main risks to the creek. Fencing, a culvert crossing and native planting are planned.

Nutrients.activities: Fertiliser application, nutrient budgeting, and soil testing
Nutrients.description: Nitrogen and phosphorus fertiliser is applied in spring and early summer to support pasture and winter crops. Rates are set from soil tests and a nutrient budget prepared each autumn.
Nutrients.risks: The main freshwater risk is nitrate leaching through the stony soils of the light soils and terraces. Autumn and winter nitrogen is avoided and no fertiliser is applied within the marked setbacks from the creek.

Point sources.activities: Chemical and fuel storage, and offal pits
Point sources.description: Chemicals and fuel are kept in a locked, bunded shed away from waterways. Farm rubbish is taken off site. There is no dairy shed, so no collected animal effluent is generated.
Point sources.risks: One old offal pit sits on the terraces and will be relocated before it is used again.

Irrigation.activities: Centre pivot irrigation, border-dyke irrigation, and water metering
Irrigation.description: Water from one consented bore is applied by two pivots, a lateral and a small border-dyke block. Irrigation is scheduled from soil moisture readings and the weekly farm water balance.
Irrigation.risks: Over-application on the lighter soils can carry nitrate below the root zone, so application depths are matched to soil water holding and the border-dyke block is being reduced.

cant.s7.irrigation.obj1.summary: Irrigation is scheduled to soil moisture and the system is checked every year.

cant.s7.irrigation.t1.not_applicable_reason: No new irrigation system is planned on this farm.

cant.s7.irrigation.t2.how_met: The pivots and the lateral are checked before the season and a uniformity test is done every year.
cant.s7.irrigation.t2.records: Annual system check; uniformity test reports

cant.s7.irrigation.t3.how_met: Irrigation is scheduled from soil moisture probes and the weekly water balance; application depth is set for each soil.

cant.s7.irrigation.t4.how_met: The owner and the part-time worker are trained by the irrigation supplier each spring.

cant.s7.soils.obj1.summary: Cultivation and winter grazing are planned to keep soil on the farm.

cant.s7.soils.t1.how_met: Winter grazing is planned around critical source areas and the creek flats are only grazed in dry conditions.

cant.s7.soils.t2.how_met: Cultivation is timed for dry soils, paddocks are re-sown before 31 March and stock come off wet paddocks at an agreed trigger.

cant.s7.waterbodies.obj1.summary: The creek and spring-fed drain are fenced, planted and kept clear of stock.

cant.s7.waterbodies.t1.how_met: The creek is fenced on one side; the remaining 400 m will be fenced by 1 March 2027.

cant.s7.waterbodies.t2.how_met: A 10 m grass margin is kept and 0.8 ha of the creek margin will be planted in natives.

cant.s7.waterbodies.t3.how_met: A culvert crossing will replace the ford at the main race; troughs are kept 20 m from the creek.

cant.s7.waterbodies.t4.how_met: Tuna and kōura habitat in the creek is protected by fencing, shade planting and no fertiliser in the setbacks.

cant.s7.point_sources.obj1.summary: One offal pit, to be moved; farm rubbish leaves the farm.

cant.s7.point_sources.t1.how_met: Farm rubbish is taken off site; the old offal pit will be moved more than 50 m from the bore and waterways before it is used again.
cant.s7.point_sources.t1.records: Pit location on the farm map

cant.s7.water_use.obj1.summary: Stock water is metered and leaks are fixed quickly.

cant.s7.water_use.t1.how_met: Stock water is float-controlled and leaks are fixed within a week; the main meter is verified every five years.

cant.s7.audit.history.issues_raised: Creek margin fencing incomplete; offal pit within 50 m of the bore.

cant.s7.extra.mahinga_kai.management: Keep the creek and spring-fed drain fenced and shaded, and keep fertiliser and chemicals out of the setbacks.

switched_off.reason: No dairy shed or stand-off pad, so no animal effluent or solid animal waste is collected on this farm.
